newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Palm Oil - Asia prices seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Palm Oil - Asia prices seen mixed.

text.p: Asian palm oil prices are likely to be mixed this week due to differing views on supplies across the region.
Traders in Singapore predicted a firmer trend after reports of a poor Indonesian crop and a shortage of ships for the transport of oil. But traders in Indonesia said prices might be steady to lower.
In Malaysia, traders said local palm oil was expected to retain last week's gains and trade in a range.
Malaysia's benchmark third month February futures contract would probably remain firm, they said.
"I don't think prices will go below 1,200 ringgit," one trader in Singapore said.
The February futures contract closed four ringgit higher from the previous day at 1,212 ringgit a tonne on Friday.
"Talk of a big drop in November production because of the start of rains could limit the downside," a trader from a Kuala Lumpur brokerage said.

Last week, Malaysian crop forecaster Ivan Wong had estimated output in November would fall by 13 percent to 770,000 tonnes from a month ago, and end-November stocks were seen holding at 980,000 tonnes, below the one million tonnes expected by the market.
Traders said they were waiting for the November 1-25 palm oil exports data from cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) Malaysia Sdn Bhd on Monday, to gauge market direction.
They also expected fresh export business next week.
Market players had mixed views on talk of a fall in Indonesian output.

"We're hearing reports that the crop in Indonesia is quite bad," the general manager of a Singapore-based commodity house said. He said production in some areas was reported to have declined by up to 15 percent.
"This is going to provide a firm undertone to the market. There have been several deferrals of exports and the squeeze in prices for November may well stretch into December," he said.
But other Singapore traders said they had received no immediate confirmation on reports that Indonesian output had dropped.
They said prices for nearby months would firm mainly because of the tight shipping situation rather than talk of a fall in Indonesian output.
Indonesian traders said olein prices would be steady to lower on weak demand but the downside could be limited by relatively high local crude palm oil prices.
"I see some downside potential next week for olein," one trader in Indonesia said.
"Some players are selling aggressively, taking profits, and this is putting pressure on prices." The trader said prices could edge downwards to 1,400 rupiah this week, where support should emerge.
Indonesian palm olein finished last week at 1,425-30 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, up from 1,415 rupiah a week ago.
Other traders said the thin margin between crude palm oil and olein prices could see players stepping up exports of the palm oil because of good export prices.
"If the margin gets any narrower, crude palm oil exports are bound to increase," an Indonesian trader said.
(With contributions from K.T. Arasu in Jakarta and Rene Pastor in Singapore)
($1 = 2.53 ringgit, $1 = 2,350 rupiah)
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230-7510)
